title: A Songbird Hangs Mice on Barbed Wire and Waits Two Days to Eat

scenes.text: A songbird hangs mice on barbed wire. It has a reason.
The loggerhead shrike is mockingbird-sized and kills mice, lizards and birds nearly its own weight.
No talons. So it grabs the neck and shakes at six g, like whiplash in a car crash.
Then it impales the body on a thorn or barbed wire, tugging it down so it stays.
Some prey is toxic. Lubber grasshoppers would sicken it fresh.
So it hangs them up for a day or two until the poison breaks down. Then it eats.

description:
A songbird that hangs mice on barbed wire, and the reason is colder than it looks.
The loggerhead shrike has no talons, so it grabs prey by the neck and shakes it at about 6 g, which researchers compare to whiplash in a car crash (Biology Letters, 2018). It then impales the body on thorns or barbed wire. Toxic lubber grasshoppers would make it sick fresh, so it leaves them hanging for one to two days until the toxins break down (Evolutionary Ecology, 1992).
Which bird do you think is the most ruthless hunter?
subject: loggerhead shrike
first_comment: A 1987 record describes a shrike killing a cardinal only two grams lighter than itself. Which songbird would you never have suspected of this?
